value.name: Marylin calms down after crying
value.description: Marylin sits in the den after crying at home and is now tearful but no longer psychotic.
evidence: Marylin sits in the den. She's had some coffee and, although teary and disheveled, is no longer psychotic.
MARYLIN I just cried when I got home.

value.name: Marylin confesses feeling judged
value.description: Marylin explains that Miles's disdain and other people's accusations have made her question how others see her.
evidence: Somehow, your disdain for me -- I'm pretty tough Miles, but I'm human.
All my life people have been ascribing these terrible motives to me.
I used to think they were jealous, or they didn't understand, but... I dunno. Maybe others see something in me. Something I'm not even aware of.

value.name: Marylin thanks Miles for hosting her
value.description: Marylin thanks Miles for letting her come to his home and admits she may have been drunk.
evidence: Anyway, thank you for letting me come here.
I guess I was a little drunk.

value.name: Marylin compliments Miles's home and art
value.description: Marylin softens the conversation by praising Miles's house and his Hockney lithograph.
evidence: You have a very nice home, Miles. Very inviting.
You have wonderful art. I love that lithograph. Hockney?

value.name: Miles denies having a girlfriend
value.description: Miles explains that the lithograph was a gift from a client, not a girlfriend.
evidence: MILES Yes. I just got that, actually. It was a gift.
MARYLIN From a -- girlfriend.
MILES No. No. I don't have a... no. It was from a client.

value.name: Marylin teases Miles about clients
value.description: Marylin jokes that Miles must have very grateful clients after hearing about the gift.
evidence: No kidding. I'll bet you have some very grateful clients.

value.name: Marylin notices Miles's family photo
value.description: Marylin spots a photograph of Miles with his mother and brother and asks if the child in the picture is him.
evidence: Marylin looks at a photograph Miles has on a side table. A WOMAN AND TWO SMALL BOYS.
MARYLIN Is that you?
MILES Me. Yes.
MARYLIN Oh. And that is -- mom?
MILES Yeah. Mom. Mom and brother.

value.name: Marylin praises Miles's childhood sensitivity
value.description: Marylin tells Miles he looks like he was a sensitive child with expressive eyes.
evidence: You look like you were a very sensitive child. You have expressive eyes.

value.name: Marylin compliments Miles's mother
value.description: Marylin says Miles's mother was beautiful and suggests she must be proud of him.
evidence: And your mother was very beautiful. She must be proud of you.
